en.statement: For CSI storage, an administrator names the driver in the StorageClass's provisioner field.
en.explanation: The provisioner identifies the CSI driver responsible for creating volumes.

en.statement: StorageClass parameters have standardized meanings across different CSI drivers.
en.explanation: A provisioner defines which parameters it accepts and what they mean.

en.statement: A StorageClass with reclaimPolicy unset gives dynamically provisioned volumes the Retain policy.
en.explanation: An unset reclaimPolicy defaults to Delete. Dynamically provisioned volumes inherit that policy.

en.statement: With no volumeBindingMode in its StorageClass, a new PVC is bound or provisioned before any Pod uses it.
en.explanation: An unset volumeBindingMode means Immediate: binding and dynamic provisioning happen once the PVC is created. On topology-constrained storage this ignores Pod scheduling needs and can leave Pods unschedulable.

en.statement: Setting nodeName lets a Pod trigger provisioning for its WaitForFirstConsumer claim.
en.explanation: Setting nodeName bypasses the scheduler, leaving the WaitForFirstConsumer claim Pending.

en.statement: The API server rejects a StorageClass whose mountOptions include an invalid filesystem option.
en.explanation: Kubernetes accepts unvalidated mountOptions; an invalid option causes the volume mount to fail.

en.statement: With several default StorageClasses, a PVC omitting storageClassName gets the newest one.
en.explanation: When more than one class carries the is-default-class annotation, claims that name no class use the newest of those default classes.

en.statement: An administrator supplies pre-created local PersistentVolumes for claims using local storage.
en.explanation: Kubernetes v1.35 provides static provisioning for local volumes rather than dynamic provisioning.

en.statement: Since Kubernetes v1.34, CSI drivers with ModifyVolume support change attributes through VolumeAttributesClass.
en.explanation: VolumeAttributesClass changes driver attributes of an existing CSI volume.

en.statement: The API server stores a PersistentVolume in the namespace of its bound PersistentVolumeClaim.
en.explanation: PersistentVolumes have cluster scope; binding to a namespaced claim does not change their scope.

en.statement: A PersistentVolumeClaim can bind to a matching PersistentVolume larger than the claim's request.
en.explanation: The binder gives a claim at least what it asked for, possibly a larger PV, and the binding is exclusive, so the extra capacity stays with that one claim.

en.statement: After a claim is deleted, a Retain PersistentVolume becomes Available for a replacement claim.
en.explanation: A Retain volume becomes Released and needs administrator reclamation before another claim can use it.

en.statement: An administrator changes a PersistentVolume's reclaim policy by patching the existing volume.
en.explanation: kubectl patch updates the policy on the existing PersistentVolume.

source.title: Change the Reclaim Policy of a PersistentVolume

en.statement: A PersistentVolumeClaim's volumeName overrides the PersistentVolume's access-mode requirements.
en.explanation: The control plane still validates access modes when a claim pre-binds through volumeName.

en.statement: Deleting a PersistentVolume still bound to a PVC leaves it Terminating until that binding ends.
en.explanation: The kubernetes.io/pv-protection finalizer postpones PV removal while the PV is bound to a PVC, so the PV shows Terminating in the meantime.

en.statement: Kubernetes can enforce filesystem write restrictions through access modes after mounting a volume.
en.explanation: Access modes guide volume matching; they do not enforce write protection after mounting.

en.statement: The scheduler derives a local PersistentVolume's node from the volume's directory path.
en.explanation: A local PersistentVolume needs nodeAffinity to identify the nodes that can access its storage.

en.statement: Raising a bound PV's capacity by hand, then its PVC's request to match, leaves the volume at its old size.
en.explanation: Kubernetes sees matching PV and PVC sizes and concludes the volume was already grown by hand, so no resize runs. To expand a bound volume, edit only the PVC.

en.statement: The node controller sets Ready to False when it loses contact with a healthy node.
en.explanation: After heartbeat silence exceeds the monitoring grace period, the node controller sets Ready to Unknown.

en.statement: By default, the kubelet renews its node Lease far more often than it rewrites an unchanged Node .status.
en.explanation: Leases are lightweight heartbeats. With default intervals, the kubelet writes .status only on a change or after a much longer interval, which cuts API load in large clusters.

en.statement: The scheduler reads a node's DiskPressure condition directly to decide whether to place a Pod there.
en.explanation: The scheduler evaluates the corresponding node taint rather than reading DiskPressure as a scheduling filter.

en.statement: DaemonSet Pods automatically receive an unlimited-duration toleration for node.kubernetes.io/unreachable.
en.explanation: The DaemonSet controller gives these Pods indefinite tolerations so temporary reachability problems leave them bound.

en.statement: The StatefulSet controller creates a replacement Pod when the original Pod's node becomes unreachable.
en.explanation: The original StatefulSet Pod remains in the API until deletion completes or an administrator intervenes.

en.statement: The kubelet tries unused-image cleanup before evicting Pods when image storage faces disk pressure.
en.explanation: The kubelet first tries image cleanup to recover storage before terminating end-user Pods.

en.statement: The kubelet honors a Pod's terminationGracePeriodSeconds when a hard eviction threshold is met.
en.explanation: For a hard eviction threshold, the kubelet terminates selected Pods immediately rather than honoring their grace period.

en.statement: In a kubeadm cluster, systemd runs the kubelet as a host service rather than as a static Pod.
en.explanation: The kubeadm package installs a systemd drop-in for the kubelet at /usr/lib/systemd/system/kubelet.service.d/10-kubeadm.conf, so systemd, not the kubelet's own manifest directory, starts and restarts it.

source.title: Configuring each kubelet in your cluster using kubeadm

en.statement: When an administrator runs kubectl cordon, Kubernetes evicts the Pods already running on that node.
en.explanation: kubectl cordon marks the node unschedulable while leaving its existing Pods running.

en.statement: The kubelet recreates a control-plane static Pod when an edit to its manifest changes the container image.
en.explanation: Updating a file in /etc/kubernetes/manifests tells the kubelet to restart that component's static Pod with the new specification.

en.statement: A control-plane static Pod can mount a Secret by referencing the Secret in its manifest.
en.explanation: A static Pod specification cannot refer to API objects such as Secrets.

en.statement: During a kube-scheduler outage, new Pods awaiting node assignment stay Pending.
en.explanation: The remaining control-plane components do not replace the missing scheduling process.

en.statement: While every kube-controller-manager instance is down, a newly created Deployment still gets a ReplicaSet.
en.explanation: The Deployment controller runs inside kube-controller-manager, so the stored Deployment gets no ReplicaSet until an instance of that process runs again.

en.statement: Running containers can continue executing during a kube-apiserver outage.
en.explanation: The kubelet maintains existing containers even when the cluster API is unavailable.

en.statement: During etcd quorum loss, kube-apiserver can persist new Pod objects through a healthy minority member.
en.explanation: etcd rejects state writes after losing its majority, even if some members remain healthy.

en.statement: The API server controls a static Pod's containers through the Pod's mirror object.
en.explanation: The mirror exposes the static Pod through the API; the local kubelet controls its containers.

en.statement: An administrator can inspect control-plane containers with crictl during a kube-apiserver outage.
en.explanation: crictl talks to the node's container runtime, so inspecting its containers does not need the cluster API.

en.statement: The kubelet treats manifests ending in .backup as inactive copies in /etc/kubernetes/manifests.
en.explanation: The kubelet reads files regardless of extension, except dot-prefixed names. Keep backup manifests outside the watched directory.

en.statement: Current metrics-server releases collect node and Pod usage from each kubelet's `/metrics/resource` endpoint.
en.explanation: The kubelet serves summarized per-node stats on /metrics/resource, and metrics-server v0.6.0 and later scrape it on every node. Older releases used the /stats/summary endpoint.

en.statement: The kubelet relies on a separate cAdvisor DaemonSet on each node to collect container resource metrics.
en.explanation: cAdvisor collection code is built into the kubelet, so the resource metrics pipeline needs no separately deployed cAdvisor workload on the nodes.

en.statement: With metrics-server installed, kube-apiserver can serve the Metrics API through the API aggregation layer.
en.explanation: Registering the Metrics API as an APIService routes resource metric requests to metrics-server.

en.statement: metrics-server writes the usage samples it collects to persistent storage, so they survive a restart of its Pod.
en.explanation: The docs describe metrics-server as lightweight, short-term and in-memory. It keeps no history, so long-term usage data needs a full metrics pipeline.

en.statement: With metrics-server installed, its resource Metrics API can report Pod filesystem usage.
en.explanation: The resource Metrics API exposes CPU and memory usage; filesystem usage needs a fuller monitoring pipeline.

en.statement: kube-scheduler uses live CPU usage to decide whether a node has room for another Pod.
en.explanation: kube-scheduler accounts for CPU requests. Low measured CPU usage does not free CPU already committed through requests.

source.title: Resource Management for Pods and Containers

en.statement: The kubelet reserves hard-eviction memory headroom when calculating Node Allocatable.
en.explanation: Memory reserved through `evictionHard` stays outside the Pod resource budget, even if system daemons reserve nothing.

source.title: Reserve Compute Resources for System Daemons

en.statement: kube-apiserver publishes its system metrics in Prometheus format for monitoring scrapers.
en.explanation: Monitoring systems scrape this text format to build component dashboards and alerts.

en.statement: A scraper reads kube-scheduler's internal metrics from kube-apiserver's `/metrics` endpoint.
en.explanation: Scrape kube-scheduler's own `/metrics` endpoint for its internal metrics.

en.statement: The container runtime sends application stdout and stderr to the node's systemd journal.
en.explanation: Container output uses CRI log files; the runtime's own logs use journald.

en.statement: A `podLogsDir` on a filesystem separate from `/var` falls outside the kubelet's disk usage tracking.
en.explanation: The kubelet supports a custom podLogsDir on the same disk as /var. On a separate filesystem it does not track that usage, so logs there can fill it up unnoticed.

en.statement: The container runtime rotates logs using its own `containerLogMaxSize` setting.
en.explanation: `containerLogMaxSize` configures the kubelet's container log rotation.

en.statement: The kubelet reads the container log file when handling a `kubectl logs` request.
en.explanation: The kubelet returns local log file contents through the API.

en.statement: The kubelet rotates log files that a static Pod component writes into a `/var/log` directory shared from the node.
en.explanation: Kubernetes does not manage rotation of logs that components write to a volume shared from the node. The node's OS or the deploy tooling has to rotate them.

en.statement: By default, the kubelet erases a container's previous logs when that container restarts.
en.explanation: The kubelet retains the preceding container's logs after a restart.

en.statement: By default, the kubelet removes a Pod's container logs from the node when it evicts the Pod.
en.explanation: Eviction removes Pod containers and their local logs.

en.statement: A streaming sidecar that copies an app's log file to its own stdout can double the node storage those logs use.
en.explanation: The app's file and the sidecar's stdout copy both sit on the node. For an app that writes a single file, the docs suggest /dev/stdout as its destination.

en.statement: A sidecar running a logging agent such as fluentd makes the logs it ships visible through `kubectl logs`.
en.explanation: An agent sidecar ships logs straight to its logging backend, outside the kubelet's control, so kubectl logs cannot show them. Read them in the backend.

en.statement: By default, kubeadm init deploys kube-proxy as a systemd service for the cluster's Linux nodes.
en.explanation: kubeadm init installs kube-proxy through the API server as a DaemonSet. Inspect that workload to locate its Pods.

en.statement: An administrator checks kube-proxy's startup logs to identify the active Service proxy mode on a failing node.
en.explanation: kube-proxy reports its selected proxy mode in startup logs, helping an administrator choose the appropriate node-level checks.

en.statement: In iptables mode, kube-proxy installs Service forwarding rules in the kernel of each node in the cluster.
en.explanation: Inspect the rules on the affected node when debugging Service forwarding. kube-proxy synchronizes its node's rules with cluster state.

en.statement: Before the Pod network add-on is installed, Pending CoreDNS Pods indicate a failed kubeadm initialization.
en.explanation: Pending CoreDNS Pods are expected before the administrator installs a Pod network add-on. They can be part of a successful kubeadm initialization.

en.statement: With the log plugin's default configuration, CoreDNS records received DNS queries even when they succeed.
en.explanation: The CoreDNS log plugin makes received queries visible during DNS troubleshooting, including successful lookups.

en.statement: CoreDNS can keep Service DNS records current when RBAC grants get instead of list and watch.
en.explanation: CoreDNS needs list and watch permissions on Services and EndpointSlices to discover records and follow their changes.

en.statement: An administrator fixes CoreDNS forwarding loops by pointing kubelet's resolv-conf at a systemd-resolved stub.
en.explanation: Point kubelet's resolv-conf at /run/systemd/resolve/resolv.conf to supply upstream resolvers. The stub can create a forwarding loop.

en.statement: With an overlay network add-on, a Pod CIDR may safely overlap the subnet that the nodes use.
en.explanation: The kubeadm docs warn, with no exception for any add-on, that the Pod network must not overlap any host network: problems are likely if it does.

en.statement: The NetworkPolicy API leaves undefined whether an ipBlock ingress rule sees the client IP or a source-NATed address.
en.explanation: Source NAT may happen before or after NetworkPolicy processing, depending on network plugin, cloud provider and Service implementation, so an ipBlock rule may match a node or load balancer IP.

en.statement: After `kubectl rollout undo` on a DaemonSet, the restored ControllerRevision keeps its original revision number.
en.explanation: DaemonSet revisions only roll forward: rolling back from revision 2 to revision 1 turns the restored ControllerRevision into revision 3.

source.title: Perform a Rollback on a DaemonSet

en.statement: With RollingUpdate, a StatefulSet's partition lets the controller update Pods at or above that ordinal.
en.explanation: During a partitioned StatefulSet rollout, Pods below the partition retain the earlier template.

en.statement: With Secret encryption configured, kube-apiserver uses the first listed provider for new Secret writes.
en.explanation: Provider order in EncryptionConfiguration determines how kube-apiserver stores new Secret writes.

en.statement: When an administrator enables Secret encryption, kube-apiserver also rewrites previously stored Secrets.
en.explanation: Existing Secrets keep their stored representation until rewritten. An administrator can use kubectl replace to apply the new encryption configuration.

en.statement: The HorizontalPodAutoscaler controller runs within the kube-controller-manager process.
en.explanation: The kube-controller-manager process hosts the controller that reconciles HorizontalPodAutoscaler objects.

en.statement: The HPA can compute CPU utilization from usage when a target Pod's CPU requests are unset.
en.explanation: The HPA needs CPU requests to compute utilization. Missing requests leave utilization undefined for that metric.

en.statement: With multiple working metrics, an HPA chooses the largest replica count proposed by those metrics.
en.explanation: The HPA evaluates metrics separately and selects the greatest proposed replica count, subject to its configured bounds.

en.statement: The HPA's scale-down stabilization uses the highest replica recommendation in its configured window.
en.explanation: Scale-down stabilization considers recent recommendations to prevent a brief drop in demand from immediately removing replicas.

en.statement: kubeadm init installs the VerticalPodAutoscaler controller as a standard cluster add-on.
en.explanation: VerticalPodAutoscaler is a separate add-on that an administrator installs in the cluster.

en.statement: A PodDisruptionBudget can block an administrator's direct `kubectl delete pod` request.
en.explanation: Direct Pod deletion bypasses PodDisruptionBudget checks; use the Eviction API for budget enforcement.

en.statement: Involuntary Pod disruptions count against the available disruption budget.
en.explanation: A failed node can consume a PodDisruptionBudget's allowance even though the budget cannot prevent the failure.

en.statement: The Kubernetes documentation recommends `AlwaysAllow` for a PodDisruptionBudget's unhealthy Pod eviction policy.
en.explanation: A PodDisruptionBudget using AlwaysAllow lets a drain evict unhealthy Pods instead of waiting for a misbehaving application to recover.

en.statement: A required node affinity rule makes the kubelet evict a running Pod when node labels stop matching.
en.explanation: A scheduled Pod continues running when node labels stop matching an `IgnoredDuringExecution` affinity rule.

en.statement: kube-scheduler combines separate `nodeSelectorTerms` with AND when evaluating node affinity.
en.explanation: Matching any `nodeSelectorTerms` entry satisfies that set of node affinity terms.

en.statement: For a Pod with `nodeSelector` and required node affinity, kube-scheduler selects a node satisfying both.
en.explanation: A Pod with nodeSelector and required node affinity needs a node that meets both constraints.

en.statement: A Pod using `preemptionPolicy: Never` ranks below lower-priority Pods in kube-scheduler's queue.
en.explanation: Non-preempting Pods retain their priority rank in the scheduling queue.

en.statement: After kube-scheduler preempts a Pod, the kubelet honors that Pod's graceful termination period.
en.explanation: Victim Pods get time to shut down before they disappear, creating a scheduling gap.

en.statement: kube-scheduler moves running Pods to repair topology spread after a workload scales down.
en.explanation: Topology spread constraints guide new placement; removing Pods can leave running Pods unevenly distributed.

en.statement: A ClusterRoleBinding can grant a user access to a non-resource URL such as `/healthz`.
en.explanation: The referenced ClusterRole specifies the URL and permitted request verbs.

en.statement: An administrator can switch a RoleBinding's role by patching its `roleRef` with `kubectl patch`.
en.explanation: `roleRef` is immutable; changing the referenced role requires deleting and recreating the binding.

en.statement: kube-apiserver treats permission to create RoleBindings as enough to grant access beyond the creator's permissions.
en.explanation: Binding a Role beyond the creator's permissions needs explicit bind authorization.

en.statement: The control plane overwrites rules an administrator adds manually to an aggregated ClusterRole.
en.explanation: Aggregation derives its rules from ClusterRoles matching its label selectors.

en.statement: The default `view` ClusterRole includes read access to Secrets stored in the assigned namespace.
en.explanation: `view` excludes Secrets because reading them can expose stronger credentials.

en.statement: The default `edit` ClusterRole covers changes to Roles and RoleBindings in its target namespace.
en.explanation: `edit` omits permissions for viewing or changing Roles and RoleBindings.

en.statement: By default, kube-apiserver restores missing permissions in default ClusterRoles when it starts.
en.explanation: Startup auto-reconciliation repairs these default RBAC rules.

en.statement: RBAC allows a resourceNames-limited list only when the request has a matching metadata.name field selector.
en.explanation: When a Role limits list or watch with resourceNames, the client has to send a matching metadata.name field selector, for example kubectl get configmaps --field-selector=metadata.name=my-cm.

en.statement: The client certificate in kubeadm's `admin.conf` places its user in the `system:masters` group.
en.explanation: `admin.conf` uses `kubeadm:cluster-admins`, whose `cluster-admin` permission comes through RBAC.

en.statement: A kubeadm administrator may reuse a product_uuid across nodes when their hostnames and MAC addresses differ.
en.explanation: kubeadm's host prerequisites include unique hostname, MAC address and product_uuid values. Duplicate machine identities can cause installation failures.

en.statement: Before `kubeadm init`, the administrator enables host IPv4 forwarding on a Linux node used for IPv4 Pod networking.
en.explanation: kubeadm init's preflight checks fail unless /proc/sys/net/ipv4/ip_forward is 1, and the Pod network add-on is installed only afterwards, so the administrator sets net.ipv4.ip_forward first.

en.statement: `kubeadm init` asks the administrator to choose a runtime when it detects several CRI sockets on the host.
en.explanation: Automatic runtime detection errors when kubeadm finds several runtimes. An explicit CRI socket tells kubeadm which runtime the node should use.

source.title: Installing kubeadm: Installing a container runtime

en.statement: `kubeadm init` installs the kubelet executable alongside the control plane's static Pod manifests.
en.explanation: The administrator installs the kubelet separately. kubeadm configures an already installed kubelet while bootstrapping the cluster.

source.title: Installing kubeadm: Installing kubeadm, kubelet and kubectl

en.statement: By default, `kubeadm init` gives the control-plane node a taint with the NoSchedule effect.
en.explanation: The node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane taint keeps the scheduler from placing Pods there unless they tolerate it.

source.title: Creating a cluster with kubeadm: Control plane node isolation

en.statement: `kubeadm join` uses the discovery CA certificate hash to authenticate the joining kubelet to the control plane.
en.explanation: The discovery hash pins the control plane's root CA public key. The TLS bootstrap token authenticates the joining node during certificate enrollment.

source.title: kubeadm join: Token-based discovery with CA pinning

en.statement: After `kubeadm certs renew`, the administrator restarts control plane Pods so components load renewed certificates.
en.explanation: Manual renewal updates certificate files. Restarting the control plane Pods ensures components use the renewed credentials because certificate reload support is incomplete.

source.title: Certificate Management with kubeadm: Manual certificate renewal

en.statement: By default, `kubeadm certs renew` rotates the cluster CA during control plane certificate renewal.
en.explanation: kubeadm certs renew signs replacement component certificates using the existing CA. kubeadm has no built-in procedure for rotating or replacing the cluster CA.

source.title: Certificate Management with kubeadm: Certificate authority rotation

en.statement: `kubeadm reset` clears the iptables rules that kube-proxy installs on the node for Service traffic.
en.explanation: kubeadm reset leaves the host's kube-proxy traffic rules in place. An administrator performs any desired rule cleanup separately.

en.statement: An administrator uses `kubeadm upgrade apply` for the first control plane node in an upgrade.
en.explanation: The first control plane node uses kubeadm upgrade apply; later control plane nodes use kubeadm upgrade node.

en.statement: The pkgs.k8s.io repository for the current minor release supplies packages for the next minor release.
en.explanation: pkgs.k8s.io has a separate repository for a minor release. Switch repositories to obtain the next minor's packages.

en.statement: An administrator must drain a node before upgrading its kubelet to a new Kubernetes minor version.
en.explanation: Draining clears evictable workloads from the node before the kubelet's minor upgrade.

en.statement: The installed CNI plugin receives its version upgrade from `kubeadm upgrade apply`.
en.explanation: The administrator upgrades the installed CNI plugin through its provider's procedure.

en.statement: The version skew policy allows the kubelet to run up to three minor versions newer than kube-apiserver.
en.explanation: The kubelet may be up to three minor versions older than kube-apiserver. A newer kubelet is unsupported.

en.statement: The version skew policy lets kubectl run one minor version newer or older than kube-apiserver.
en.explanation: kubectl's supported minor-version window extends in both directions relative to kube-apiserver.

en.statement: `etcdutl snapshot restore` sends snapshot data to a running etcd member over the network.
en.explanation: etcdutl snapshot restore reads a local snapshot file and creates a restored data directory.

en.statement: After an etcd restore to a new directory, the administrator updates the static Pod's etcd-data hostPath.
en.explanation: Point the etcd-data hostPath in /etc/kubernetes/manifests/etcd.yaml at the restored host directory.

en.statement: In a stacked HA cluster, losing a control plane node can also take an etcd member offline.
en.explanation: Stacked topology places an etcd member and control plane components on the same host, so host failure affects both.

en.statement: By default, `helm install` applies new CRDs from `crds/` before creating an operator chart's custom resources.
en.explanation: Helm registers definitions from crds/ before submitting chart resources that use those newly defined kinds.

en.statement: During a chart upgrade, Helm upgrades the operator's CRDs stored in its `crds/` directory.
en.explanation: Helm leaves existing `crds/` definitions untouched during upgrades; an administrator manages their changes separately.

en.statement: Before `kubectl apply -k` can install an add-on overlay, an administrator installs the standalone kustomize binary.
en.explanation: kubectl has supported kustomization files since v1.14, so kubectl kustomize and kubectl apply -k work without a separate kustomize binary.

source.title: Declarative Management of Kubernetes Objects Using Kustomize

en.statement: For Pod network setup, the container runtime loads the installed CNI plugins on the node.
en.explanation: The administrator configures the container runtime to load the CNI plugins used for Pod networking.

en.statement: With a runtime exposing a legacy CRI API instead of CRI v1, the kubelet can still register the node.
en.explanation: A runtime needs CRI v1 support for kubelet node registration; an older CRI API alone is insufficient.

en.statement: The Kubernetes documentation recommends CNI plugins compatible with the CNI v1.0.0 specification.
en.explanation: A plugin can support several CNI specification versions while remaining compatible with CNI v1.0.0.

en.statement: With differing request and storage versions, kube-apiserver saves a new custom resource in the request version.
en.explanation: kube-apiserver stores custom resources in their CRD's designated storage version, regardless of the request version.

en.statement: After creating a CRD, an administrator can check `Established` to see when its API endpoint becomes usable.
en.explanation: A true `Established` condition signals that the custom resource endpoint is ready for requests.

source.title: Extend the Kubernetes API with CustomResourceDefinitions

en.statement: An operator's controller normally runs inside the control plane, alongside kube-controller-manager.
en.explanation: The operator pattern page says the controller normally runs outside the control plane like any containerized app, for example as a Deployment in the cluster.

en.statement: A Pod using `hostNetwork: true` can reach the node's loopback listeners using `localhost`.
en.explanation: A hostNetwork Pod shares the node's network namespace, so its loopback address reaches listeners in that host namespace.

en.statement: An application's `localhost` listener stays isolated from other containers in the same Pod.
en.explanation: Containers in a Pod share its IP address and port space. A loopback listener is reachable from the Pod's other containers.

en.statement: With a Pod network add-on installed, the kubelet can reach local Pods through their Pod IPs.
en.explanation: The network model includes connectivity from node agents to Pods on that node, which lets the kubelet contact local Pods.

en.statement: For a dual-stack Pod, an administrator gets its complete address inventory by reading `status.podIP`.
en.explanation: status.podIP records a primary address. The assigned IPv4 and IPv6 addresses appear together in status.podIPs.

en.statement: An administrator deploys a NetworkPolicy in the namespace containing the Pods it protects.
en.explanation: A NetworkPolicy selects its protected Pods within its own namespace.

en.statement: Kubernetes sets a `kubernetes.io/metadata.name` label on every namespace, so a namespaceSelector can match it by name.
en.explanation: The control plane sets this immutable label with the namespace name as its value, so a NetworkPolicy can target one namespace without custom labels.

en.statement: An administrator can target a Service directly by name in a NetworkPolicy egress rule.
en.explanation: NetworkPolicy selects traffic peers by Pod or namespace labels, or by IP ranges; Service names are outside its API.

en.statement: A NetworkPolicy supports client-certificate requirements for connections to selected Pods.
en.explanation: NetworkPolicy controls network traffic at the IP and port level. Client-certificate checks need a TLS-aware implementation.

en.statement: NetworkPolicy automatically records denied connections in its standard API for an administrator to inspect.
en.explanation: Per-connection logging is outside the NetworkPolicy API. Denial logs depend on the networking implementation.

en.statement: From Kubernetes v1.33 on, each allocated Service ClusterIP references an IPAddress object in the Kubernetes API.
en.explanation: The allocator, stable since v1.33, replaces the internal allocation map with ServiceCIDR objects for the ranges and IPAddress objects for each IP, so administrators can run kubectl get ipaddresses.

en.statement: In Kubernetes v1.35, kube-proxy's ipvs proxy mode is deprecated.
en.explanation: The kernel IPVS API fits the Services API poorly. The docs recommend nftables mode, stable since v1.33 and needing kernel 5.13 or later, as the replacement for ipvs.

en.statement: For external NodePort traffic with `externalTrafficPolicy: Local`, kube-proxy replaces the client's source IP.
en.explanation: With externalTrafficPolicy set to Local, kube-proxy preserves the external client's source IP for NodePort traffic.

en.statement: With `internalTrafficPolicy: Local`, kube-proxy sends ClusterIP traffic to remote endpoints if local ones are absent.
en.explanation: For internalTrafficPolicy Local, kube-proxy drops ClusterIP traffic when the client node has no local endpoint.

en.statement: With cloud-controller-manager, creating a LoadBalancer Service synchronously provisions the external load balancer.
en.explanation: cloud-controller-manager provisions the load balancer asynchronously and publishes its details in the Service's .status.loadBalancer.

en.statement: `kubeadm init` configures CoreDNS by storing its Corefile in a Secret in the kube-system namespace.
en.explanation: CoreDNS reads its Corefile from the coredns ConfigMap in kube-system. Administrators edit that ConfigMap to change server configuration.

en.statement: By default, `kubeadm init` exposes CoreDNS Pods through a Service named `kube-dns` in the kube-system namespace.
en.explanation: The kube-dns Service name preserves compatibility for workloads across DNS implementations.

en.statement: The kubelet configures a Pod using `dnsPolicy: Default` with resolver settings inherited from its node.
en.explanation: dnsPolicy Default makes Pod name resolution follow the node's resolver configuration.

en.statement: The kubelet applies `ClusterFirstWithHostNet` when a hostNetwork Pod leaves `dnsPolicy` unset.
en.explanation: Leaving dnsPolicy unset gives a Pod ClusterFirst, and a hostNetwork Pod with ClusterFirst falls back to the Default policy, so set ClusterFirstWithHostNet explicitly.

en.statement: A Gateway API administrator sets a GatewayClass's controllerName to the controller's Kubernetes Deployment name.
en.explanation: A GatewayClass's controllerName holds the implementation's assigned controller identifier. It identifies a Gateway API implementation rather than a Kubernetes Deployment object.

en.statement: An administrator can assign different GatewayClass objects to different listeners of the same Gateway API Gateway.
en.explanation: A Gateway names its GatewayClass through spec.gatewayClassName. Its listeners share that class and the infrastructure that implements it.

en.statement: By default, a Gateway API controller considers all compatible Gateway listeners for an HTTPRoute's parentRef.
en.explanation: A Gateway parentRef targets the Gateway's listeners by default. An administrator uses sectionName to restrict that reference to a named listener.

en.statement: Attaching an HTTPRoute to a Gateway in another namespace needs that listener's allowedRoutes to permit it.
en.explanation: A Route's parentRefs requests a Gateway attachment. The listener's allowedRoutes must also admit the Route's namespace for cross-namespace attachment.

en.statement: A ReferenceGrant in the HTTPRoute's own namespace allows its backendRefs to a Service in another namespace.
en.explanation: The ReferenceGrant belongs in the referenced Service's namespace. The owner of that namespace grants source HTTPRoutes permission to reference its Services.

en.statement: With a Gateway API controller, an HTTPRoute can split traffic between Service backends using relative weights.
en.explanation: An HTTPRoute backend's share is its weight divided by the sum of the rule's backend weights. The weights express ratios rather than fixed percentages.

en.statement: With a Gateway API controller, an HTTPRoute specifies the certificate Secret for its Gateway listener's TLS termination.
en.explanation: A Gateway listener's TLS configuration selects the certificate Secret through certificateRefs. TLS termination configuration belongs to the Gateway.

en.statement: With multiple Ingress controllers running, an administrator uses ingressClassName to select the handling controller.
en.explanation: An Ingress resource's ingressClassName names an IngressClass associated with an installed controller.

source.title: Ingress Controllers: Using multiple Ingress controllers

en.statement: Kubernetes continues adding new standard routing features to the Ingress API alongside Gateway API development.
en.explanation: The Ingress API is frozen, so its standard feature set has stopped growing. It remains a supported, generally available Kubernetes API.
